terms.gloss: a rule, a regulation; a condition
evidence: Cic. Amic. 44: haec igitur prīma lēx amīcitiae sanciātur
terms.comment: Besides the laws of the state, any rule laid down for how a thing is done (Lewis & Short: “a law, precept, regulation, principle, rule”). eā lēge ut, on condition that (Plaut. Most. 2.1.13, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.110: nostrae nātūrae rēgulā mētiāmur
terms.comment: Properly a ruler (see ruler), then a standard to measure by. Traupman uses it for rules in general: rēgulam servāre, to keep the rule; rēgulam frangere, to break it (pp. 372–373).

evidence: Cic. Off. 2.51: hoc praeceptum officiī dīligenter tenendum est
Sen. Ep. 6.5: longum iter est per praecepta
terms.comment: A rule given as advice or instruction, by a teacher or a parent.

phrases.latin: haec igitur prīma lēx amīcitiae sanciātur, ut ab amīcīs honesta petāmus, amīcōrum causā honesta faciāmus
phrases.english: let this, then, be the first rule of friendship: to ask friends only for what is right, and to do only what is right for their sake

sources: Lewis & Short: lex · Lewis & Short: regula · Lewis & Short: praeceptum
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 248, 372–373.
Cicero’s Laelius and Seneca from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-philosophica, loci-seneca-epistulae); De officiis checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
